name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_PBLOCKELEMENTS_MCQ_Q01 - Basicity and boiling point of Group 15 hydrides

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Among the hydrides of Group 15 elements, \(\mathrm{NH_3}\) is the strongest base and \(\mathrm{BiH_3}\) is the weakest base.

Statement II: \(\mathrm{NH_3}\) has a higher boiling point than \(\mathrm{PH_3}\) because \(\mathrm{NH_3}\) molecules are associated through intermolecular hydrogen bonding.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The basicity of Group 15 hydrides (\(\mathrm{EH_3}\)) depends on the availability of the lone pair on the central atom \(\mathrm{E}\), while boiling points depend on the strength of intermolecular forces.

Step 2: Evaluation of Both Claims
Down Group 15 from \(\mathrm{N}\) to \(\mathrm{Bi}\), atomic size increases and the lone pair is dispersed over a larger volume, so basicity decreases in the order \(\mathrm{NH_3} > \mathrm{PH_3} > \mathrm{AsH_3} > \mathrm{SbH_3} \ge \mathrm{BiH_3}\); thus \(\mathrm{NH_3}\) is the strongest base and \(\mathrm{BiH_3}\) is the weakest. Furthermore, due to the small size and high electronegativity of nitrogen, \(\mathrm{NH_3}\) forms intermolecular hydrogen bonds in the liquid state, whereas \(\mathrm{PH_3}\) does not, giving \(\mathrm{NH_3}\) a higher boiling point (\(238.5\ \mathrm{K}\) vs \(185.5\ \mathrm{K}\)).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both statements are chemically accurate and correct.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_PBLOCKELEMENTS_MCQ_Q02 - Electronic configuration and boiling points of noble gases

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: All Group 18 elements except helium have the general valence shell electronic configuration \(ns^2np^6\).

Statement II: Helium has the highest boiling point among all noble gases because of strong dispersion forces.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Noble gases have completely filled valence shells, and their physical properties such as boiling point depend on the magnitude of weak dispersion forces between monoatomic atoms.

Step 2: Evaluation of Both Claims
All Group 18 elements possess an \(ns^2np^6\) valence configuration except helium, which has \(1s^2\); hence the first claim is correct. However, helium is the smallest noble gas with minimal polarisability and weakest dispersion forces, so it has the lowest boiling point (\(4.2\ \mathrm{K}\)) of any known substance rather than the highest; hence the second claim is incorrect.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The claim regarding the valence electronic configuration of Group 18 elements is correct, whereas the claim regarding helium having the highest boiling point is incorrect.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_PBLOCKELEMENTS_MCQ_Q03 - Covalency and single bond strength in nitrogen vs phosphorus

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Nitrogen forms pentahalides such as \(\mathrm{NCl_5}\) because it can expand its covalency using vacant \(2d\) orbitals.

Statement II: The single \(\mathrm{N-N}\) bond is stronger than the single \(\mathrm{P-P}\) bond, giving nitrogen a greater tendency for catenation than phosphorus.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Second-period elements (\(n = 2\)) have only \(2s\) and \(2p\) orbitals (no \(2d\) orbitals), restricting maximum covalency to 4. Single homonuclear bond strength in small atoms is affected by lone pair–lone pair repulsion.

Step 2: Evaluation of Both Claims
Nitrogen lacks \(d\)-orbitals in its valence shell, so it cannot expand its covalency beyond 4 and does not form pentahalides like \(\mathrm{NCl_5}\). Additionally, because of the small \(\mathrm{N-N}\) bond length, non-bonding electrons on adjacent nitrogen atoms experience high interelectronic repulsion, making the single \(\mathrm{N-N}\) bond weaker than the single \(\mathrm{P-P}\) bond and resulting in weaker catenation in nitrogen.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both statements are incorrect.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_PBLOCKELEMENTS_MCQ_Q04 - Reactivity and structure of white and red phosphorus

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Red phosphorus is much more reactive than white phosphorus and glows in the dark.

Statement II: White phosphorus consists of discrete tetrahedral \(\mathrm{P_4}\) molecules with \(\mathrm{P-P-P}\) bond angles of \(60^\circ\), leading to angular strain.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The chemical reactivity of phosphorus allotropes is governed by their molecular structures and internal bond-angle strain.

Step 2: Evaluation of Both Claims
White phosphorus is much more reactive than polymeric red phosphorus and exhibits chemiluminescence (glows in the dark), whereas red phosphorus is far less reactive and does not glow in the dark; thus the first claim is incorrect. White phosphorus consists of discrete tetrahedral \(\mathrm{P_4}\) molecules with \(60^\circ\) bond angles, which creates angular strain and accounts for its high reactivity; thus the second claim is correct.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The claim about red phosphorus being more reactive and glowing in the dark is incorrect, while the structural explanation for white phosphorus is correct.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_PBLOCKELEMENTS_MCQ_Q05 - Reducing property of H3PO2 and disproportionation of H3PO3

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Hypophosphorous acid (\(\mathrm{H_3PO_2}\)) is a good reducing agent because it contains two \(\mathrm{P-H}\) bonds.

Statement II: Orthophosphorous acid (\(\mathrm{H_3PO_3}\)) on heating disproportionates to give orthophosphoric acid (\(\mathrm{H_3PO_4}\)) and phosphine (\(\mathrm{PH_3}\)).

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
In oxoacids of phosphorus, \(\mathrm{P-H}\) bonds impart reducing character, and intermediate oxidation states (such as \(+3\)) undergo disproportionation on heating.

Step 2: Evaluation of Both Claims
\(\mathrm{H_3PO_2}\) has one \(\mathrm{P=O}\), one \(\mathrm{P-OH}\), and two \(\mathrm{P-H}\) bonds; the two \(\mathrm{P-H}\) bonds make it a strong reducing agent capable of reducing \(\mathrm{AgNO_3}\) to metallic silver. Furthermore, \(\mathrm{H_3PO_3}\) (oxidation state \(+3\)) disproportionates on heating according to \(4\mathrm{H_3PO_3 \rightarrow 3H_3PO_4 + PH_3}\) into \(+5\) and \(-3\) states.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both statements are correct.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_PBLOCKELEMENTS_MCQ_Q06 - Contact process catalyst and dissociation constants of H2SO4

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In the Contact Process, the catalytic oxidation of \(\mathrm{SO_2}\) to \(\mathrm{SO_3}\) by \(\mathrm{O_2}\) is carried out in the presence of \(\mathrm{V_2O_5}\) as a catalyst.

Statement II: In aqueous solution, the second acid dissociation constant (\(K_{a_2}\)) of \(\mathrm{H_2SO_4}\) is much greater than its first acid dissociation constant (\(K_{a_1}\)).

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The key step of the Contact Process is \(2\mathrm{SO_2(g) + O_2(g) \xrightarrow{V_2O_5} 2SO_3(g)}\). For diprotic acids, the first dissociation is generally much stronger than the second.

Step 2: Evaluation of Both Claims
\(\mathrm{V_2O_5}\) is indeed the catalyst used in the Contact Process for oxidising \(\mathrm{SO_2}\) to \(\mathrm{SO_3}\). However, in water, \(\mathrm{H_2SO_4}\) dissociates almost completely in the first step (\(K_{a_1} > 10\)) to \(\mathrm{H_3O^+}\) and \(\mathrm{HSO_4^-}\), whereas the second dissociation of \(\mathrm{HSO_4^-}\) to \(\mathrm{SO_4^{2-}}\) is much smaller (\(K_{a_2} = 1.2 \times 10^{-2}\)), so \(K_{a_2} \ll K_{a_1}\).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The claim regarding the Contact Process catalyst is correct, whereas the claim regarding \(K_{a_2} > K_{a_1}\) is incorrect.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_PBLOCKELEMENTS_MCQ_Q07 - Electron gain enthalpy and oxidising power of fluorine vs chlorine

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The negative electron gain enthalpy of fluorine is more negative than that of chlorine.

Statement II: Chlorine is a stronger oxidising agent than fluorine in aqueous solution.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Electron gain enthalpy is influenced by atomic size and interelectronic repulsions in the valence shell, while aqueous oxidising power depends on bond dissociation enthalpy, electron gain enthalpy, and hydration enthalpy.

Step 2: Evaluation of Both Claims
Due to the very small size of the fluorine atom and strong interelectronic repulsions in its compact \(2p\) orbitals, the negative electron gain enthalpy of fluorine (\(-333\ \mathrm{kJ\ mol^{-1}}\)) is less negative than that of chlorine (\(-349\ \mathrm{kJ\ mol^{-1}}\)). Moreover, \(\mathrm{F_2}\) (\(E^\circ = +2.87\ \mathrm{V}\)) is a much stronger oxidising agent than \(\mathrm{Cl_2}\) (\(E^\circ = +1.36\ \mathrm{V}\)) because of the low \(\mathrm{F-F}\) bond dissociation enthalpy and high hydration enthalpy of \(\mathrm{F^-}\).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both statements are incorrect.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_PBLOCKELEMENTS_MCQ_Q08 - Hydrolysis of XeF6 and molecular structure of XeF4

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Partial hydrolysis of \(\mathrm{XeF_6}\) to form \(\mathrm{XeOF_4}\) and \(\mathrm{XeO_2F_2}\) is a redox reaction in which xenon is reduced.

Statement II: \(\mathrm{XeF_4}\) has a square planar molecular structure with four bonding pairs and two lone pairs on the central xenon atom.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
A redox reaction requires a change in oxidation states, while molecular geometry is predicted by VSEPR theory from the number of bonding pairs and lone pairs.

Step 2: Evaluation of Both Claims
In the partial hydrolysis of \(\mathrm{XeF_6}\) (\(\mathrm{XeF_6 + H_2O \rightarrow XeOF_4 + 2HF}\) and \(\mathrm{XeF_6 + 2H_2O \rightarrow XeO_2F_2 + 4HF}\)), the oxidation state of xenon remains \(+6\) throughout, so it is not a redox reaction; hence the first claim is incorrect. In \(\mathrm{XeF_4}\), xenon has 8 valence electrons forming 4 \(\mathrm{Xe-F}\) bonding pairs and 2 lone pairs, which occupy opposite axial positions of an octahedron to give a square planar molecular structure; hence the second claim is correct.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The claim that partial hydrolysis of \(\mathrm{XeF_6}\) is a redox reaction is incorrect, while the structural description of \(\mathrm{XeF_4}\) is correct.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
